Chemtrade Logistics Announces $80 Million Expansion to Boost Canadian Chemical Production

Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund has unveiled plans for an $80 million expansion of its sulphuric acid production facility in Sarnia, Ontario, aiming to strengthen its position in the Canadian chemicals sector and meet growing demand from key industrial customers.

The expansion, scheduled to be completed by late 2026, is expected to increase site capacity by 25 percent and create approximately 60 construction jobs at its peak. Upon completion, the company anticipates adding 15 permanent roles to its operations team in Sarnia.

“This investment reflects our commitment to supporting Canada’s manufacturing base and providing reliable supply to our customers,” said Mark Hanley, Chief Executive Officer of Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund. “We are seeing increased demand from sectors such as mining, fertilizer, and water treatment, and this project will enhance our ability to serve those core markets.”

Industry analysts note that the expansion comes as the chemicals sector faces robust demand for high-purity sulphuric acid and related products. “This is a strategic move for Chemtrade,” said Dana Lin, an analyst at Northbridge Capital Markets. “Capacity increases like this help stabilize supply chains and support downstream industries across Ontario and beyond.”

The Sarnia facility, in operation since 1978, is among the region’s largest producers of sulphuric acid and its derivatives. According to the Chemical Industry Association of Canada, sulphuric acid is a critical input for a range of sectors, from agriculture to battery manufacturing. Local officials welcomed the investment, citing its potential to generate economic benefits for the region.

“Chemtrade’s expansion will provide good jobs for our community and reinforce Sarnia’s reputation as a hub for chemical manufacturing,” said Mayor Jim Bradley. “We look forward to working with Chemtrade as the project moves forward.”

Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund reported annual revenues of $1.7 billion in 2023. The company stated that it will fund the expansion through a mix of cash flow and existing credit facilities, without plans to alter its current dividend policy.
